name: MIRA
note: Studio Gang 2020, 40 storeys: its own geometry, a stack of triangular bay windows whose apexes slide floor by floor so the bays spiral (the grammar's `bays` face draws one fixed plan on every floor). way/693630796 is the tower part inside the MIRA outline way/939499092, which carries the mid-rise wing (see "MIRA (Folsom wing)"). Web: 400 ft, ten bay geometries, 14 ft wide, 6.5 ft deep, thirty per level; white metal and glass.

name: MIRA (Folsom wing)
note: Tower grammar: MIRA's six-storey wing on Folsom, cream and dark-red panels over a dark-red base (street views way-939499092.jpg, way-693630796.jpg). The OSM outline is tagged 129 m because it contains the tower part; the wing itself is ~22 m.

name: Hilton San Francisco Financial District
note: Reworked 2026-10-16 from Commons photos + LiDAR (docs/shots/refs/notable/hilton-fidi): tower on the east 63 m only, glazed ribbed slab between blank end pylons with twin stacks, everything flaring over the bottom storeys; Kearny podium where the skybridge lands. Was: Tower grammar (concrete-piers): Clement Chen with John Carl Warnecke, 1971, the Brutalist hotel slab over Portsmouth Square — tan concrete piers, slot windows, deep parapet, two roof boxes. OSM says 111 m / 32 levels; it is 27 storeys and 298 ft, so 91 m (Wikipedia, confirmed by the street views).

name: 101 Second Street
note: Tower grammar + a limestone shaft: SOM 1999, 26 storeys, 108 m — a pale green glass office volume beside the stone service core, which rises past the roof under a glass veil over the plant. OSM leaves it unnamed and splits the complex into parts (this is the tall one).

name: 655 Montgomery Street
note: Tower grammar (granite-eighties): the Montgomery-Washington Tower, 1984, 26 storeys — buff precast, dark teal glass, the top storeys stepping back to their terraces (street view way-256072715.jpg for the buff panels and the dark canopy; way-256072715-2.jpg is aimed at the Transamerica Pyramid, not this building).
